summary: Inserts node a2 at the tail of a doubly linked list. Reads the list head stored at this[62] (offset 0xF8); when the head is non-null it walks next pointers at +440 to the last node and links a2 in as the new tail (previous at +436, next at +440). When the head is null it makes a2 the new head. Returns the node that became the tail (or the new head on the empty-list path).

operations.description: Load the list head pointer from dword index 62 (offset 0xF8) of this into the traversal cursor.
If the loaded head is non-null, enter the traversal-and-append path; otherwise take the empty-list branch that makes a2 the head.
Walk from the starting node referenced via this[172] (offset 0x2B0), following next pointers at +440 until the node whose next pointer is zero is reached, keeping that node as the tail.
Write the new node a2 into the tail node's next pointer at +440.
Write the previous tail node into a2's previous pointer at +436.
Clear a2's next pointer at +440 to zero so it terminates the list.
On the empty-list path, promote a2 to be the new list head stored at this[62] (offset 0xF8).
On the empty-list path, clear a2's previous pointer at +436 to zero.
On the empty-list path, clear a2's next pointer at +440 to zero.
Return the node that now terminates the list: the appended tail on the full-list path, or a2 on the empty-list path.
